setup.scope: This market covers the value of dedicated gaming console hardware sold at retail or direct-to-consumer, including home consoles (e.g., PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch) and handheld/portable consoles, whether new or officially refurbished, measured as the end-user purchase value of the console device itself. It excludes software, games, subscriptions, accessories, controllers, and cloud/streaming gaming services, which are separately valued markets, and it excludes general-purpose devices such as smartphones, PCs, and smart TVs even when used for gaming. Console-packaged bundles are counted only at the console's own hardware value, with bundled software or accessory value stripped out. Console software and service demand may be used as an intermediate signal for how many consoles are required (e.g., attach-rate evidence), but software and services are never priced or valued as part of this market.

setup.scope: This market covers the value of dedicated gaming console hardware (home and handheld/portable consoles and their first-party hardware variants) sold at wholesale/retail to end users, including new-generation and prior-generation console units. It excludes software, subscriptions, accessories, and services (e.g., games, online memberships, controllers sold separately), which are separately valued markets, and excludes PC gaming hardware, mobile gaming devices, and general-purpose computing devices. Refurbished/resold consoles are excluded from the primary market value, though they may be referenced as a secondary signal for installed-base and replacement demand. Console unit shipments and installed-base data are used as the physical volume anchor, with revenue derived from average selling prices per unit.
